pages.text:
Rina’s school gate was always busy after class.

Children ran out with bags, bottles, lunch boxes, and half-finished stories. Sometimes one shoe came untied. Sometimes someone’s cap flew away.

Near the yellow wall, one boy stood every day.

His name was Ari.

He was new in school. He did not play much. He did not talk much. He just stood near the gate and watched the crowd.

“Why does he stand there?” asked Pooja.

“Maybe he thinks he is too important,” said Dev.

Rina was not sure.

One day, she saw Ari pick up a little pink hairclip from the ground. He dusted it and placed it safely on the wall.

Another day, a small child dropped her water bottle. Ari picked it up and gave it back, then quickly stepped away.

That did not look proud to Rina.

On Thursday, the sky became dark. Rain clouds came over the school.

Children rushed toward the gate.

Just then, Dev slipped on a mango leaf.

His arms went up.

His bag went sideways.

His lunch box flew open, and one lonely potato roll rolled across the ground.

Everyone laughed.

Dev sat up and said, “I meant to do that.”

Rina laughed too, then looked at Ari.

He was not laughing. He was watching the junior block.

A little girl with two short braids stood near the steps. She looked scared of the crowd.

Rina walked to Ari.

“Hi,” she said. “Why do you stand here every day?”

Ari looked surprised.

“I wait for my sister,” he said. “She gets scared when everyone runs. If I stand here, she knows where to find me.”

Rina felt sorry for thinking wrongly.

The little girl dropped her bottle. Rina picked it up.

“Are you Ari’s sister?” she asked kindly.

The girl nodded.

“Come,” Rina said. “We will walk slowly.”

Ari smiled. “Thank you.”

Dev came limping over, holding his lunch box.

“What are you doing?” he asked.

“Helping,” said Rina.

Dev looked at Ari’s sister.

“Oh,” he said softly.

The next day, Rina stood near the yellow wall too. Pooja joined her. Even Dev came, still checking the ground for mango leaves.

When Ari’s sister came out, the crowd did not seem so scary.

Ari smiled.

Rina smiled back.

Ari had not been proud.

He had been kind in a quiet way.
